title: MakeMyTrip reports $286 Mn revenue in Q1 FY27; profit plunges 65%
summary:
Online travel platform MakeMyTrip reported a mixed performance for the first quarter of FY27, with revenue growing in single digits while profit declined 65% to $9.1 million due to higher finance costs linked to its convertible notes.
The Nasdaq-listed company recorded 6.2% year-on-year growth in revenue to $285.6 million in the quarter ended June 2026 from $268.8 million in the corresponding period last year. In constant currency terms, revenue grew 16.1%.
MakeMyTrip said the quarter was affected by a more than 10% depreciation in the Indian rupee against the U.S. dollar, as well as subdued international outbound travel due to the ongoing West Asia conflict. However, strong domestic travel demand helped offset part of the impact.
Hotels and packages remained the company's largest business with revenue of $151.2 million, recording a 6.7% year-on-year increase. Bus ticketing revenue climbed 15.9% to $44.9 million. Revenue from the air ticketing segment fell 7.5% to $55.6 million, while the others segment recorded 19.6% growth to $33.9 million.
Gross bookings grew 9.4% to $2.85 billion, led by growth across hotels, bus ticketing and air travel. Hotel room nights rose nearly 20% to 12.8 million, while bus ticket volumes increased 23.9% to 43.6 million.
On the expense front, service costs rose 10.4% year-on-year to $82.7 million, driven by strong demand for packages and car bookings in India. Marketing and sales promotion expenses increased 11.1% to $48.8 million, while other operating expenses edged up 2.3% to $65.3 million. Personnel expenses, however, declined 3.4% to $38.8 million.
Finance costs surged to $35 million in Q1 FY27 from $10.8 million a year earlier, primarily due to higher interest expenses on convertible senior notes. As a result, net finance costs jumped to $28.3 million from $4 million in the year-ago quarter.
In the end, the Gurugram-based company reported a 64.7% decline in profit to $9.1 million during the quarter, as higher finance costs weighed on its bottom line. Its Adjusted EBITDA stood at $55.5 million during the quarter.
As of June 30, 2026, MakeMyTrip held $370.7 million in cash and cash equivalents and $423.6 million in term deposits.

title: Beyond earnings: Pine Labs rewrites POS playbook, bets on Blinkit and Zepto for gift cards
summary:
While investors focused on Pine Labs' quarterly earnings and guidance, the company's first post-listing earnings call offered a deeper look at the strategy shaping its next phase of growth. Beyond the headline numbers, the fintech company disclosed a new economics for its POS business, revealed that its credit-processing business has quietly grown into a nearly Rs 100 crore annual revenue stream, and outlined plans to expand gift card distribution through Blinkit and Zepto. 
Management also shared updates on its AI initiatives, new issuing products and international expansion, providing fresh insight into how Pine Labs is evolving beyond its core payments business.
A new playbook for POS economics
Perhaps the biggest structural change outlined during the earnings call relates to Pine Labs' terminal business.
For years, the company purchased POS devices and leased them to merchants, earning recurring rental income. That model is now changing. Pine Labs said nearly 25-30% of new terminal deployments now require merchants to purchase the hardware upfront instead of the company carrying it on its own balance sheet.
While this lowers reported contribution margins because hardware sales are inherently low-margin, management said the strategy reduces depreciation, improves cash efficiency and creates a lighter balance sheet.
The company expects to deploy 125,000-130,000 terminals during the year, with most network investments already completed.
A Rs 100 Cr business hidden in plain sight 
Another notable disclosure was around Pine Labs' issuing platform.
Management revealed that its credit issuing and acquiring processing business has grown into an annual revenue business of nearly Rs 100 crore, a figure it has not previously highlighted publicly.
The company said its issuing platform today spans nearly 20 countries, extending well beyond gift cards into prepaid cards, forex cards and open-loop payment products.
To further expand the business, Pine Labs plans to launch meal cards, fuel cards and expense cards by October, while also building direct-to-consumer prepaid products.
Blinkit and Zepto become Pine Labs' new gift card storefronts
Pine Labs also revealed that it has started distributing gift cards through Blinkit and Zepto, signalling that quick commerce is becoming an important sales channel for digital gifting.
The company is simultaneously expanding into gaming by distributing Roblox gift cards and targeting in-app purchases, which management sees as another growth avenue.
Interestingly, despite multiple analyst questions on gift cards, issuing and distribution, management made no reference to breakage income, unredeemed gift cards or breakage accounting, instead focusing on processing, distribution and new products.
AI and global expansion power the next phase 
Alongside these strategic shifts, Pine Labs continued to outline its investments in AI and overseas markets.
The company said nearly 90% of new code across several business divisions is now written using AI-assisted tools, while it recently demonstrated what it called India's first agentic payment, where AI agents completed a payment transaction using UPI mandates.
Internationally, Pine Labs said it has won British Airways for its gift card platform, deployed 30,000 terminals with GCash in the Philippines and is expanding operations across Singapore and the UAE.
Despite reporting its first profitable year, Pine Labs continues to invest in growth, adding 500 sales employees over the past six months to strengthen merchant acquisition and enterprise sales. Notably, the company made no mention of engineering or technology hiring,
Taken together, the earnings call painted a picture of Pine Labs expanding beyond its core payments business through new POS economics, a growing issuing platform, AI investments and international expansion. Yet one aspect remained conspicuously absent. Despite extensive discussions around gift cards, issuing and processing, management made no reference to breakage income, unredeemed gift card balances or related accounting practices. Instead, the focus remained firmly on new distribution channels such as Blinkit and Zepto, processing capabilities and the launch of new prepaid products.

title: Exclusive: Spinny converts into public company; FY26 topline touches Rs 6,000 Cr
summary:
Used car retailing platform Spinny is preparing for its planned initial public offering (IPO) by converting into a public company.
The board has passed a special resolution to change the name of its parent entity from Valuedrive Technologies Private Limited to Valuedrive Technologies Limited, a move that typically precedes a public listing, according to regulatory filings accessed by Entrackr.
According to a recent Bloomberg report, Spinny has appointed Kotak, Morgan Stanley, and Citi as lead bankers for an IPO in CY27.
Founded in 2015 by Niraj Singh and Mohit Gupta, Spinny operates a full stack used car marketplace, offering vehicle buying, selling, financing, insurance, and after sales services. The company also owns Truebil and completed the acquisition of auto service platform GoMechanic in 2024. It further expanded its portfolio with the acquisition of Autocar India, an automotive media and car content platform, in March 2025.
According to sources, Spinny is currently selling close to 15,000 cars every month. The company serves car buyers across 25 cities and enables car sellers from more than 100 cities.
Sources also said Spinny plans to expand its buyer footprint to around 35 cities in the near term by adding 10 more locations.
For the fiscal year ended March 2025, Spinny's revenue from operations grew 25% year on year to Rs 4,657 crore from Rs 3,730 crore in FY24. According to sources, the company is expected to close FY26 with revenue of around Rs 6,000 crore.
Entrackr has reached out to Spinny for comments.
Spinny has raised approximately $780 million to date, with Tiger Global and Accel among its largest shareholders. The company last raised around $165 million from Accel Leaders Fund, Fidelity Investments, and other investors at a valuation of $1.5 billion to $1.8 billion.

title: Ather Energy reports Rs 1,217 Cr revenue in Q1 FY27, loss drops to Rs 51 Cr
summary:
Electric two-wheeler manufacturer Ather Energy announced its Q1 FY27 results today. During the period, the company reported 89% year-on-year growth in its operating revenue. At the same time, the losses for the Bengaluru-based company narrowed by 71% to Rs 51 crore.
Ather’s revenue from operations rose to Rs 1,217 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 645 crore in Q1 FY26, according to its quarterly report sourced from the National Stock Exchange (NSE).

The sale of electric two-wheelers and related services remained Ather Energy's sole source of operating revenue, although the company did not disclose a detailed revenue breakup. During the quarter, it sold 88,655 vehicles, up 9% quarter-on-quarter from 81,072 units in Q4 FY26.
The company also recorded Rs 43 crore in other income, taking its total income for the quarter to Rs 1,260 crore.
Ather's largest expense continued to be the cost of materials, primarily battery cells and other components, which surged 88% year-on-year to Rs 977 crore in Q1 FY27 and accounted for nearly 75% of the company's total expenditure. Employee benefit expenses remained largely unchanged at Rs 118 crore during the quarter.
Depreciation and amortisation charges, along with spending on legal, advertising, and other operating expenses, pushed the company's total expenditure to Rs 1,311 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 851 crore in the year-ago quarter.
Higher electric two-wheeler sales helped Ather significantly improve its bottom line during the quarter. The company more than doubled its vehicle sales to 88,655 units from 41,083 units in Q1 FY26, which contributed to a 71% decline in net loss to Rs 51 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 178 crore in the year-ago quarter.
According to Vahan data, Ather Energy retained its third position in July despite a 8.3% decline in registrations to 28,819 units and 14.89% market share.
Last month, Ather approved a Rs 1,200 crore preferential issue, with existing investor Hero MotoCorp committing nearly Rs 960 crore. The India-Japan Fund (IJF) will invest Rs 200 crore, while the company's promoters will contribute the remaining Rs 40 crore.
At the end of today’s trading session, Ather’s share price closed at Rs 1,280, with a total market capitalization of Rs 50,448 crore or $5.3 billion.

title: Transition VC-backed Matel raises Rs 130 Cr in Series B round led by UC Impower
summary:
Pune based Matel Motion & Energy Solutions has raised Rs 130 crore (around $15 million) in a Series B funding round led by UC Impower. The round also saw Catamaran join as a new investor, while existing investor Transition VC also participated.
In May 2024, Matel had raised $4 million in its Series A round led by Transition VC and others.
The fresh capital will be used to expand manufacturing capacity, strengthen research and development, accelerate product development, increase hiring across engineering and production teams, and support the company's international expansion.
Founded in 2017 by Sunil Patel and Netaji Patro, Matel designs and manufactures motors, motor controllers, and integrated powertrains for automotive and industrial applications.
The startup offers solutions for a wide range of electric vehicles, including two wheelers, three wheelers, four wheelers, buses, and off road vehicles. It commenced mass production of its powertrains in April 2024 after receiving validation and certification from multiple EV OEMs.
Its products are used across electric vehicles, pumping and cooling systems, and other industrial applications.
The company has also developed magnet free motor technology and offers IE5 industrial motors, while an IE6 motor is under development. Matel currently supplies products to multiple OEMs across the two wheeler, three wheeler, and industrial segments.
Founder and CEO Sunil Patel previously led the Chetak EV development programme at Bajaj Auto's R&D division, while co founder Netaji Patro has held R&D roles at Maruti Suzuki and Bajaj Auto.

title: Imarticus Learning acquires Singapore-based BELLS Institute of Higher Learning
summary:
Professional education company Imarticus Learning has acquired Singapore based BELLS Institute of Higher Learning.
The acquisition brings together two institutions focused on professional education and workforce development. Imarticus Learning, which says it has served over 1 million learners, joins BELLS' network of more than 150,000 alumni, seven training centres across Singapore, and its collaborations with the Singapore government, SkillsFuture Singapore, and enterprises across the region.
The combined organisation has more than 1,100 employees and operates from over 25 offices across India and Singapore.
While Imarticus Learning has built a presence in finance and professional education in India, BELLS adds capabilities in enterprise learning, artificial intelligence (AI), data analytics, technology, and workforce development, along with relationships with the Singapore government.
According to the company, the acquisition will provide Indian learners with access to Singapore exchange opportunities and ASEAN career pathways, while learners in Singapore will gain access to Imarticus Learning's programmes in finance, data science, analytics, and technology.
The combined entity plans to offer programmes spanning AI literacy, applied machine learning, AI for finance and fintech, and AI enabled business transformation. The programmes will be developed in collaboration with industry partners and aligned with employer demand across Singapore, India, and the broader ASEAN region.
Co-founded by Nikhil Barshikar and Sonya Hooja, Imarticus Learning offers undergraduate education through the Imarticus School of Finance & Business (ISFB), along with career launch programmes, Prodegrees, global certifications, executive education, corporate learning, and government skilling initiatives.

summary:
AI startup Sarvam is set to raise $74 million (around Rs 700 crore) in an extension of its Series B round, led by NVIDIA Corporation, with participation from Glade Brook Capital, Gaja Capital, Indigo Ventures, and other investors.
The development comes soon after Sarvam raised $234 million in a round led by HCL Technologies, which propelled the company to unicorn status.
The Sarvam AI’s board passed a special resolution to approve the issuance of 20,244 Series B preference shares and 7 equity shares at an issue price of  Rs 3,44,570 each to raise Rs 698 crore or $74 million, according to its filing with the Registrar of Companies (RoC).

Other participants, including angel investors and family offices such as Vrijesh Agarwal, KJ Trust, and AL Trust.
In March, Moneycontrol reported that NVIDIA and other investors were in talks to invest in Sarvam AI.
Founded by Vivek Raghavan and Pratyush Kumar, Sarvam develops AI models, inference infrastructure, and enterprise AI products tailored for Indian languages and use cases. The startup has recently released several foundational models trained from scratch in India, including Sarvam 105B, Sarvam 30B, and Sarvam Vision
According to Entrackr’s analysis, the firm will be valued at around Rs 14,342 crore or $1.51 billion post-money. 
Following the allotment of this tranche, NVIDIA Corporation will hold a 1.66% stake in the company, while Glade Brook Capital will own 1.33%. HCL Technologies' stake will be diluted to 9.95%, while the founders will retain a 38.44% stake in the company.

title: Astrotalk Store claims Rs 1 Cr daily GMV, launches dedicated gemstones platform
summary:
Astrotalk's e-commerce arm Astrotalk Store has reached a daily GMV run rate of around Rs 1 crore and processed 1.6 million orders in 2025, according to the company. It has also launched a dedicated platform for gemstones as it looks to expand its presence in the spiritual products segment.
Launched in November 2024, Astrotalk Store sells spiritual and wellness products such as Rudraksha, Pyrite, crystal jewellery, zodiac bracelets, Vastu products, spiritual combos and yantras. The company said the business was incubated with an initial investment of Rs 30 lakh to test the category.
The company attributed the demand for these products to recommendations made during astrology consultations. It added that the store was created to offer an organised marketplace with a focus on sourcing and authenticity.
Astrotalk has now launched a standalone platform for gemstones. According to the company, the platform offers precious and semi precious stones with lab certification, astrological consultation and a replacement policy. It believes the category remains fragmented due to limited transparency around sourcing and certification.
The company also added that it adds more than 30 products every month across categories. Anmol Jain, co-founder of Astrotalk, said the company has focused on sourcing, merchandising and new product launches over the past year. He added that the dedicated gemstones platform is intended to build customer trust in the category.
GoKwik, which provides checkout solutions to Astrotalk Store, said the brand has recorded consistent growth on its platform and has built an organised online marketplace for spiritual commerce.
Earlier this year, Astrotalk had announced that its e-commerce vertical generated more than Rs 140 crore in revenue in 2025 and was operating at an annualised revenue run rate of over Rs 200 crore. The company had also disclosed an additional investment of Rs 40 crore to scale inventory, strengthen its supply chain and expand product categories. At the time, Astrotalk Store offered more than 300 SKUs and outlined plans to add another 500 products by FY27.

title: Coffee equipment and services provider Kaapi Machines raises Rs 50 Cr from Sedna HoReCa
summary:
Coffee equipment and services provider Kaapi Machines has secured an equity infusion of Rs 50 crore from Sedna HoReCa (Sedna), a private equity backed B2B HoReCa solutions provider, while also entering into a strategic partnership.
The partnership is expected to expand Kaapi Machines' product portfolio, strengthen its manufacturing capabilities, and enhance its technology stack, warehousing, and service infrastructure.
The company also plans to explore select opportunities in adjacent product categories for its existing customer base by leveraging Sedna's capabilities.
Led by Abhinav Mathur, Kaapi Machines serves coffee businesses and the broader farm to cup coffee ecosystem. Its clients include large café chains, QSRs, specialty coffee roasters, hotels, retailers, corporates, and coffee vending businesses across India.
With coffee consumption continuing to grow in India, the company aims to support both existing and new HoReCa businesses through its product portfolio, training programs, R&D capabilities, and after sales support.
Kaapi Machines supplies equipment including automatic and semi automatic espresso machines, commercial blenders, roasters, and grinders. It is the official distributor for brands such as La Marzocco, Mahlkönig, Rancilio, and Probat. The company also offers barista training, latte art courses, consulting for new cafés, technical maintenance and repair services, and operates the Something's Brewing e-commerce platform for home brewers.

title: MobiKwik reports Rs 281 Cr revenue and Rs 7.6 Cr profit in Q1 FY27
summary:
Fintech platform MobiKwik announced its quarterly results today. The company reported a marginal increase in operating revenue and turned profitable, posting a net profit of Rs 7.6 crore in the quarter, compared to a net loss of Rs 42 crore in the corresponding quarter last year.

MobiKwik's revenue from operations increased 3.7% year-on-year  to Rs 281 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 271 crore in Q1 FY26, its unaudited financial statements accessed from the National Stock Exchange (NSE) show.

The company’s total income stood at Rs 289 crore in Q1 FY27, compared to Rs 282 crore a year earlier.
For MobiKwik, commissions from recharges and loan servicing, along with income from payment gateway and technology platform services, were the key revenue contributors in Q1 FY27. The company, however, did not disclose a segment-wise revenue breakup in its quarterly filing.
For the Gurugram-based firm, payment processing charges continued to be the largest expense at Rs 117 crore, accounting for 41.6% of total expenses. Employee benefit expenses increased to Rs 53 crore, while lending operational expenses declined sharply to Rs 1.8 crore.
Financial guarantee expenses rose to Rs 28 crore, while other expenses stood at Rs 81 crore, taking the company's total expenses to Rs 281 crore, down 13.3% from Rs 324 crore in Q1 FY26.
The company reported a net profit of Rs 7.6 crore in Q1 FY27, compared to a net loss of Rs 42 crore in Q1 FY26, aided by lower overall expenses and a sharp decline in lending operational costs. Its EBITDA stood at Rs 16 crore during the quarter compared to Rs 31 crore EBITDA loss in Q1 FY26.
On a sequential basis, MobiKwik's operating revenue declined marginally to Rs 281 crore, while its net profit nearly doubled to Rs 7.6 crore, reflecting improved profitability despite a slight moderation in revenue.
At 11:38 AM, MobiKwik's shares were trading at Rs 290 apiece, giving the company a market capitalization of approximately Rs 1,614 crore at the time of writing.

title: 1xBet branding reaches India via FanCode, Zee, Sony LIV; accountability remains unclear
summary:
Offshore betting platform 1xBet received prominent visibility during India's recent tour of Zimbabwe, streamed in India on FanCode and Zee. Its visibility raises questions over how 1xBet branding continues to reach Indian audiences despite multiple government advisories against advertisements for offshore betting and gambling platforms.
1xBet was an official partner of the three match T20 series held from July 23 to 26 at the Harare Sports Club. Its logo appeared on perimeter boards, sight screens, backdrops and other advertising spaces at the stadium.
The visibility comes against the backdrop of multiple government measures aimed at restricting the promotion of online money gaming and offshore betting platforms. Since 2022, the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting has issued multiple advisories asking television channels, digital publishers, OTT platforms and online intermediaries not to carry advertisements, including surrogate advertisements, for offshore betting and gambling platforms.
Separately, the Promotion and Regulation of Online Gaming Act, 2025 was brought into force through a government notification issued in April this year, while the accompanying Promotion and Regulation of Online Gaming Rules, 2026 took effect on May 1.
In its partnership announcement, 1xBet specifically highlighted the availability of the matches on FanCode and Zee Entertainment and said this would ensure broad brand exposure among the T20 audience.
Entrackr has reached out to 1xBet to understand whether reaching Indian audiences through FanCode and Zee was part of its sponsorship objective, whether it had any commercial arrangement with the platforms, and its position on the branding in light of India's online gaming and advertising regulations. The story will be updated if it responds.
The 1xBet branding was visible in the live broadcast and also appeared in match clips later posted by FanCode on its social media handles.
A person familiar with the matter at FanCode told Entrackr that the platform receives the feed directly from the publisher and has no control over advertisements displayed at the ground.
FanCode declined to comment on the story.
However, while FanCode may have limited control over branding embedded in a live feed supplied by the host broadcaster, the appearance of 1xBet branding in clips later posted on its own social media channels also brings into focus whether betting related branding can be reviewed, cropped, blurred or masked before such content is redistributed.
Entrackr has also reached out to Zee regarding the visibility of 1xBet branding during the series, its role, if any, in the sponsorship arrangement, and safeguards it follows for betting related branding in overseas sports feeds. The story will be updated if it responds.
Entrackr has asked the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting whether branding for offshore betting platforms embedded in overseas sports feeds falls within existing advertising restrictions when distributed in India, and whether Indian broadcasters and streaming platforms are expected to restrict or mask such branding. The story will be updated if the ministry responds.
Section 6 of the Promotion and Regulation of Online Gaming Act, 2025 prohibits advertisements that directly or indirectly promote online money games. Entrackr has also sought clarity from the ministry on whether the provision has any bearing on branding for offshore betting platforms embedded in international sports broadcasts.
The legislation also affected India's online money gaming industry. Dream Sports, the parent company of FanCode, along with other real money gaming platforms such as Gameskraft, Zupee, WinZO and A23, discontinued paid contests after the law came into effect.
1xBet branding also visible on Sony LIV
A similar instance emerged during India A's recent tour of Sri Lanka, where 1xBet branding was prominently visible during matches broadcast in India on Sony Sports Network and Sony LIV.
Entrackr asked Sony whether it was aware of the branding, had any role in its broadcast, and what safeguards it has to restrict betting related advertisements in international feeds. Sony did not respond until the publication of this story.
The recurrence across two separate overseas tours suggests the issue is not limited to a single broadcast. It also puts the focus on the BCCI's role in overseas tours involving India and India A. While on ground advertising at overseas venues may be controlled by host boards and their commercial partners, it remains unclear whether the BCCI has guidelines or contractual safeguards concerning betting related sponsorships during matches involving Indian teams.
Entrackr reached out to the BCCI to understand its position on the 1xBet branding during both tours, whether it had raised the issue with the respective host boards, and whether it has any policy or contractual safeguards concerning betting related sponsorships during overseas tours involving Indian teams.
The BCCI did not respond until the publication of this story.
Even if stadium advertising is controlled by host boards or their commercial partners, broadcasters and streaming platforms redistribute the content to Indian audiences. The two instances raise questions over whether such platforms should review or mask betting related branding before it reaches viewers in India.

title: KKR-backed LEAP India files RHP for Rs 2,480 Cr IPO; issue opens August 7
summary:
Logistics solutions firm LEAP India Limited has filed its red herring prospectus (RHP) with SEBI for its Rs 2,480 crore initial public offering (IPO), which is scheduled to open on August 7.
The IPO will open for subscription on August 7 and close on August 11, with the anchor book opening on August 6. The company has fixed the price band at Rs 151 to Rs 159 per share.
The company received approval from the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) to launch its IPO in December last year.
According to its RHP, LEAP India has increased the fresh issue size to Rs 480 crore from the Rs 400 crore proposed in its draft red herring prospectus (DRHP) filed in August last year. The remaining Rs 2,000 crore of the IPO comprises an offer for sale (OFS).
The OFS will be led by Vertical Holdings II Pte. Ltd., a promoter entity backed by KKR, which plans to sell shares worth Rs 1,998.6 crore. Another KKR-backed promoter group entity, KIA EBT Scheme 3, will offload shares worth around Rs 13.8 crore.
Founded in 2013, EAP India provides pallet pooling, container pooling, and related material-handling solutions across industries. The company counts leading FMCG, pharma, and e-commerce players among its clients.
JM Financial, Avendus Capital, IIFL Capital, and UBS Securities are the book-running lead managers to the issue, while MUFG Intime India is the registrar.
Of the proceeds from the fresh issue, Rs 360 crore will be used to repay certain borrowings, while the remaining amount will be allocated for general corporate purposes.
As of the RHP filing date, KKR-backed Vertical Holdings II Pte. Ltd. is the company's largest shareholder with a 73.78% stake, followed by founder Sunu Mathew, who holds 21.07%. Sixth Sense Ventures, First Bridge Fund, and Madhurima International Pvt. Ltd. own 1.41%, 1.21%, and 1%, respectively.
For the fiscal year ended March 2026, Leap India reported 57% year-on-year growth in its operating revenue to Rs 730 crore from Rs 466 crore in FY25. At the same time, its profits also jumped over 70% to Rs 63 crore.

title: Urban Company shares jump 13% as Morgan Stanley upgrade, InstaHelp milestone lift sentiment
summary:
Urban Company's shares rallied nearly 13% on Monday after the company informed stock exchanges that its quick home services offering, InstaHelp, crossed 100,000 delivered orders in a single day. The stock also got a major boost after global brokerage Morgan Stanley upgraded the company to "Overweight" from "Underweight" and sharply raised its target price.
The announcement came just days after Urban Company reported a strong first quarter for FY27, with operating revenue rising 44% year-on-year. While the company remained loss-making during the quarter, investors looked past near-term earnings and focused on its improving growth trajectory.
Launched to offer faster, on-demand home services, InstaHelp has quickly emerged as one of Urban Company's biggest growth bets. Crossing the 100,000 daily orders mark highlights strong customer adoption and reinforces the company's position in the fast-growing convenience services segment.
Morgan Stanley upgraded the stock after the June quarter results, raising its target price to Rs 165 from Rs 128. The brokerage cited stronger execution, improving growth visibility and confidence that Urban Company could achieve its profitability targets earlier than previously expected. It also highlighted the rapid scale-up of InstaHelp as a key driver of the company's long-term growth potential.
The sharp rally indicates that investors are increasingly optimistic about Urban Company's ability to expand beyond its traditional home services business and build a larger convenience services platform. While the company continues to invest aggressively in scaling InstaHelp, the latest operating milestone and the brokerage's positive outlook have strengthened confidence in its long-term strategy.
Urban Company shares were trading around Rs 146 as of 10:48 AM, valuing the company at Rs 22,514 crore ($236 million).

title: EV charging startup RoadGrid secures Rs 13 Cr from Technology Development Board
summary:
EV charging technology startup RoadGrid has secured Rs 13 crore in financial assistance from the Technology Development Board (TDB) under the Department of Science and Technology for a Rs 27.5 crore manufacturing project.
The firm will use the funds to establish a manufacturing and assembly facility for its patented Universal EV Charger. 
The facility will have an annual capacity of 2,000 chargers, with commercial production expected to begin in March 2027.
Founded in 2020, RoadGrid develops EV charging hardware, software and energy management solutions. Its Universal EV Charger supports electric two-wheelers, three-wheelers, passenger vehicles and commercial EVs through a single platform.
The brand claims that its facility will manufacture and assemble components including power electronics, thermal management systems, communication modules, control hardware and metering systems. The project will use locally manufactured components and is expected to create more than 100 jobs.
RoadGrid currently employs over 40 people and has deployed more than 100 EV chargers while managing over 200 charging points. It works with six enterprise customers and has partnerships with companies including VinFast, HPCL and IOCL.
Earlier this year, RoadGrid raised Rs 12 crore in a pre-Series A funding round led by Venture Catalysts to support product development, manufacturing and charging infrastructure deployment.
The company expects the new facility to generate around Rs 100 crore in annual revenue at an initial production level of 1,000 chargers.

title: Snabbit crosses 115,000 daily jobs, says burn per job drops below Rs 250 in Q1 FY27
summary:
Quick home services startup Snabbit has crossed 115,000 fulfilled jobs in a single day, according to the company. It also reported improvements in its unit economics during the first quarter of FY27.
According to Snabbit, it completed around 4 million jobs in its core househelp category during Q1 FY27, while its consolidated Net Order Value (NOV), after accounting for customer discounts, crossed Rs 130. During the quarter, burn per job declined by more than Rs 100 quarter on quarter to below Rs 250.
The company scaled from around 400 daily jobs to more than 115,000 a day in under two years. It had crossed 50,000 daily jobs and one million monthly jobs earlier this year.
Snabbit currently operates across 10 cities including Mumbai, Delhi, Thane, Navi Mumbai, Gurgaon, Ghaziabad, Noida, Faridabad, Pune and Hyderabad, covering more than 150 micromarkets. According to the company, it continues to focus on increasing density within existing neighbourhoods to improve fulfilment efficiency and customer retention.
The company also reported early traction in newer categories such as Home Cooks and Salon at Home.
Founder and CEO Aayush Agarwal said that mature micromarkets are now completing more than 2,500 jobs a day, while several residential communities generate over 500 daily jobs. He added that the company expects its consolidated NOV to improve by another 15% to 20% over the coming months.
Snabbit currently facilitates more than 100,000 earning opportunities every day for its network of over 25,000 Experts and has enabled eShram registration for eligible workers on its platform.
The announcement comes months after Snabbit raised $56 million in a Series D funding round, taking its total capital raised to $112 million. 
The announcement comes amid growing competition in the quick home services segment. Rival Urban Company's InstaHelp also crossed 100,000 delivered orders in a single day on Sunday, reaching the milestone at 5:54 PM. The company said the final tally for the day was expected to be higher.
According to a recent Moneycontrol report, InstaHelp completed around 1.9 million orders in July, ahead of Snabbit's 1.85 million, while Pronto crossed 1.25 million bookings.
Snabbit also maintained that its growth has not been driven primarily by aggressive discounting. According to the company, its consolidated NOV crossed Rs 130 after customer discounts.

title: Urban Company’s InstaHelp crosses 100,000 daily delivered orders
summary:
Urban Company on Sunday announced that its quick service housekeeping vertical InstaHelp has crossed 100,000 delivered orders in a single day, around five months after the platform reached 50,000 daily bookings.
According to the company, InstaHelp crossed the 100,000 delivered orders milestone at 5:54 PM on August 2. The final number for the day is expected to be higher. The company added that the figure reflects peak daily deliveries, while the business will continue to focus on customer retention, service quality and the availability of service professionals for long term growth.
“Crossing 100,000 delivered orders in a single day, barely five months after we crossed 50,000, reflects both the growing consumer demand for InstaHelp and the strength of the operating model we've built. We are building this category the way we build everything at Urban Company with a strong focus on unit economics and long term value. As we scale, Net Transaction Value and contribution per order remain the metrics we hold ourselves to, because they reflect the true, durable health of the business,” said Abhiraj Singh Bhal, CEO and co-founder of Urban Company.
The announcement comes days after Urban Company disclosed its Q1 FY27 results. InstaHelp fulfilled 3.82 million orders during the quarter, up 43% from 2.67 million in Q4 FY26, while its adjusted EBITDA loss per order improved to Rs 346 from Rs 447 in the preceding quarter.
Urban Company launched InstaHelp as a pilot in Mumbai in March 2025. The platform offers housekeeping services such as cleaning, dishwashing, laundry and meal preparation, with professionals available within 10 to 15 minutes of booking. It currently operates across select micro markets in major metro cities.
In February this year, InstaHelp crossed 50,000 daily bookings, less than a year after its pilot launch. The company later said the platform completed more than 1 million monthly delivered bookings in March, with three days still left in the month.
According to a recent Moneycontrol report, InstaHelp completed around 1.9 million orders in July and regained the top position in the instant home services segment. Rival Snabbit completed around 1.85 million orders during the month, while Pronto crossed 1.25 million bookings.

title: Zepto confirms pre IPO private placement, says listing within SEBI approved timeline
summary:
Quick commerce major Zepto has officially confirmed that it will undertake a pre-IPO private placement ahead of its planned public listing, while indicating that it will continue to focus on business execution before launching its IPO.
In a statement issued on Friday, the company said it has agreed with major shareholders to close a pre IPO private placement of equity. The financing will strengthen its balance sheet, which stood at Rs 5,681 crore in cash with no debt as of March 31, 2026.
"As part of the IPO process, the Board and Founders have received terms from public market investors to list the company and are appreciative of the expressed interest. However, at this time, and afforded by the company's strong balance sheet, Zepto will focus on continued execution," the company said.
Zepto added that it will update its draft red herring prospectus (DRHP) with its operating results and financials in the coming quarters and intends to list within the timeframe permitted by SEBI under its approved UDRHP.
The announcement comes days after multiple media reports indicated that the company had postponed its IPO plans amid valuation discussions with investors. Reports had also suggested that Zepto was in talks to raise more than Rs 1,000 crore through a pre IPO placement from existing investors including Glade Brook, General Catalyst, Goodwater Capital, and Nexus Venture Partners.
Zepto had initially planned an IPO of around Rs 8,000 crore. In June, the company filed its updated DRHP with SEBI for a fresh issue of Rs 8,010 crore and subsequently received the regulator's approval. Recent reports had indicated that the company may reduce the IPO size to around Rs 5,000 crore to Rs 6,000 crore.
According to its FY26 financial statements, Zepto doubled its operating revenue to Rs 11,110 crore from Rs 5,454 crore in FY25. Its net loss, however, widened 26% to Rs 5,905 crore.

title: Indian startup funding drops to $662 Mn in July after June spike
summary:
Indian startups raised $662 million in July, a sharp decline from the blockbuster $2 billion recorded in June, when Meta's investment in CRED accounted for a significant share of the month's funding. July saw only one funding round above $100 million as Emergent raised fresh capital and became the seventh unicorn of 2026. The second largest deal stood at just $40 million, a sign of the limited availability of large ticket funding during the month. Despite the month on month decline, July's funding remained above May's $630 million. Early stage startups accounted for 38% of the total capital raised. IPO activity remained strong, although Zepto postponed its public listing amid valuation discussions with investors. The month also saw four startup shutdowns, while no major layoffs were reported separately in the media, a rare occurrence in recent months.

[Funding overview]
According to data compiled by Entrackr, Indian startups raised approximately $662 million across 85 deals in July. The total included 16 growth and late stage deals worth $410 million and 64 early stage deals worth $252 million. Additionally, five deals were disclosed without their funding amounts during the month.
[M-o-M and Y-o-Y trend]
Month on month, startup funding fell 67% to $662.2 million in July from $2 billion in June, the second lowest monthly total in the past 13 months. Year on year, funding rose 11% from $597.6 million in July 2025 to $662.2 million in July 2026, while the number of deals declined from 105 to 85.

[Top 10 growth stage deals]
Growth and late stage funding in July was led by AI startup Emergent, which raised $130 million in a Series C round. Raghu Vamsi Aerospace Group, Veriqus, and BusinessNext followed with $40 million each, while Neo Group secured $36.3 million in a Series C round. Other notable deals included Limelight Diamonds, Elevate Education, Quick Clean, Apna Mart, and Naturis Cosmetics, with investments spread across AI, fintech, deeptech, consumer, edtech, and manufacturing.

[Top 10 early stage deals]
Early stage funding in July was led by Arboreal Bioinnovations, which raised $24 million in a Series A round. Plazza and Vorflux followed with $15 million each, while Reo.Dev and BatX Energies secured $11.3 million and $11 million, respectively. Other notable deals included Dovetail Capital, Aham Housing Finance, E3 Electric.AI, CARPL.ai, and Aukera, with investments spread across foodtech, AI, fintech, mobility, healthtech, battery technology, and ecommerce.

[Mergers and Acquisitions]
M&A activity in July featured several notable transactions across ecommerce, proptech, edtech, and venture capital. Snitch acquired fashion brand Berrylush to expand its presence in women's fashion, while Aurum PropTech announced plans to acquire Housing.com in a $46.2 million deal. PhysicsWallah increased its stake in Sarrthi IAS to a majority through a $7.5 million transaction, which strengthened its presence in the civil services test preparation segment. WTF also acquired creative agency BTG, which expanded its presence in the brand and creative services space.
[City and segment wise deals]
Bengaluru retained its lead in startup funding during July, accounting for $323.93 million, or 48.92% of the total capital raised across 43 deals. Delhi NCR followed with $136.35 million from 16 deals, while Mumbai secured $100.15 million across 13 deals. Hyderabad raised $49.6 million through three deals, whereas Pune recorded $11.6 million from four transactions.
AI attracted the highest investor interest in July with 15 deals worth $201.62 million, accounting for 31.75% of the total funding raised. Fintech followed with $141.5 million across 8 deals, while ecommerce startups secured $55.15 million through 12 deals. Deeptech and edtech startups raised $43.35 million and $20.25 million, respectively.
[Stage wise deals]
Series B attracted the highest funding in July with $190.4 million across 8 deals, accounting for 28.75% of the total capital raised. Series A followed with $141.16 million from 17 deals, while Seed rounds contributed $60.97 million across 29 deals. Pre Series A and Pre Seed startups raised $30.25 million and $11.45 million, respectively.

[Layoffs, shutdowns and departures]
July saw four startup shutdowns, with Dream Money, Klydo, PicSee, and Medial ceasing operations. Unlike previous months, there were no major layoff announcements. Even so, layoffs during H1 2026 affected nearly 2,500 employees across private startups. On the leadership front, startups recorded 25 key executive hires and 6 senior level departures, indicating a continued focus on leadership expansion despite the funding slowdown.

[Trends] 
AI remained the top investment theme: AI attracted the highest investor interest in July, with 15 deals worth $201.62 million. Emergent's $130 million round and its entry into the unicorn club further strengthened the sector's momentum.
Large ticket funding remained limited: July saw only one funding round above $100 million, while the second largest deals stood at $40 million. The gap highlights the continued scarcity of large late stage investments.
Zepto's IPO delay remained a key market focus: Zepto postponed its planned IPO amid valuation discussions with investors. The decision drew significant attention as the company remains one of the most closely watched startup listing candidates.
Pronto's wearable camera program sparked industry debate: Pronto confirmed that it is expanding its wearable camera initiative through its opt-in Pronto Verified service, which records service sessions and uses anonymized footage for AI training. The move triggered discussions around privacy and the use of AI in home services.
Flipkart prepared to enter food delivery: Walmart-owned Flipkart announced plans to enter India's online food delivery market in the coming weeks. The move is expected to intensify competition for incumbents Zomato and Swiggy.

title: UPI hits highest ever monthly volume with 23.66 Bn transactions in July
summary:
Unified Payments Interface (UPI) recorded its highest ever monthly transaction volume in July 2026, with 23.66 billion transactions worth Rs 29.88 lakh crore, according to data released by the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI).
The July numbers surpassed the previous record of 23.20 billion transactions set in May this year. However, transaction value remained marginally below the all time high of Rs 29.90 lakh crore recorded in the same month.
On a daily basis, UPI processed 763 million transactions, while the average daily transaction value stood at Rs 96,383 crore.
Compared to June, transaction volume increased 4.1% from 22.72 billion, while transaction value rose 3.3% from Rs 28.92 lakh crore. On a year on year basis, transaction volume grew 22%, while transaction value increased 19%.
UPI crossed the 23 billion monthly transaction mark for the first time in May.
As of June, Walmart backed digital payments platform PhonePe retained its lead in the UPI ecosystem with 10.48 billion transactions, followed by Google Pay and Paytm in the second and third spots, respectively. Meanwhile, WhatsApp surpassed CRED in UPI transaction volume, processing 150.48 million transactions compared with 141.78 million for CRED. NPCI is yet to release the app wise transaction data for July.
Recently, the Maldives launched a real time payment corridor with India, further expanding UPI's global footprint. UPI merchant payments are now live in 10 international markets: Bhutan, Singapore, the United Arab Emirates, France, Mauritius, Sri Lanka, Nepal, Qatar, Cambodia, and the Maldives. Greece remains connected for person to person transfers, while Singapore and Nepal also support remittance linkages.

title: TVS extends lead in July as Ola Electric, Ather record decline in EV two-wheeler sales
summary:
EV two-wheeler registrations in India stayed above 1.93 lakh in July 2026. TVS Motor strengthened its leadership by crossing 50,000 registrations, while Ola Electric and Ather Energy witnessed a drop in sales.
According to the latest Vahan data, TVS Motor led the EV two-wheeler market with 52,538 registrations in July and a 27.15% market share. The company posted 10.8% month-on-month growth, with 5,125 more registrations than in June.
Bajaj Auto retained the second spot with 43,607 registrations and a 22.53% market share in July. Its registrations rose marginally from 43,504 units in June.
Ather Energy retained the third position with 28,819 registrations and a 14.89% market share in July. The company recorded an 8.3% month-on-month decline, with 2,616 fewer registrations than in June.
Hero MotoCorp ranked fourth with 21,174 registrations and a 10.94% market share in July. The company reported a marginal 3.3% month-on-month decline. 
Ola Electric remained fifth with 13,170 registrations and a 6.80% market share in July. The company recorded one of the steepest declines among the leading EV two-wheeler makers, with sales falling 19% month on month, or by 3,079 units, from 16,249 registrations in July.
Greaves Electric Mobility followed with 9,701 registrations and a 5.01% market share after its sales dropped 11.3% over June.
Among the fastest-growing players in the top 10, BGauss recorded the strongest month-on-month growth at 33.9%, with registrations rising to 5,324 units. River Mobility followed with a 24.8% increase to 5,554 units.
Among the other players, Simple Energy posted an 11.2% month-on-month growth, with registrations rising to 1,532 units in July. Lectrix EV entered the top 10 after its registrations increased 22.8% over June to 1,335 units.

title: InstaHelp earns Rs 29 per order while losing Rs 346 in Q1 FY27
summary:
Urban Company’s quick home services platform InstaHelp recorded an adjusted EBITDA loss of Rs 346 per order in Q1 FY27, an improvement from Rs 447 per order in Q4 FY26, even as its overall losses widened during the quarter.
InstaHelp’s adjusted EBITDA loss stood at Rs 132 crore in Q1 FY27 as compared to Rs 119 crore in the preceding quarter. The platform fulfilled 3.82 million orders during the quarter, up 43% from 2.67 million orders in Q4 FY26.
The platform generated Rs 11.22 crore in revenue during the quarter, up from Rs 9 crore in Q4 FY26. Its net transaction value (NTV) increased 32% quarter on quarter to Rs 52.9 crore from Rs 40.1 crore.
Launched in March 2025, InstaHelp’s NTV has grown steadily since its launch, increasing from Rs 27.6 crore in Q3 FY26 to Rs 40.1 crore in Q4 FY26 and Rs 52.9 crore in Q1 FY27. Fulfilled orders also increased from 1.6 million in Q3 FY26 to 2.67 million in Q4 FY26 and 3.82 million in Q1 FY27.
At the same time, average order value declined to Rs 138 in Q1 FY27 from Rs 150 in the previous quarter amid competitive pricing in the segment. Based on its operating revenue and fulfilled orders, InstaHelp’s revenue per order also declined to around Rs 29.4 from Rs 33.3 in the preceding quarter.
Despite the increase in absolute losses, InstaHelp’s loss per order declined nearly 23% quarter on quarter to Rs 346 from Rs 447. Urban Company attributed the improvement to higher network density as order volumes scaled. In Q3 FY26, the platform’s adjusted EBITDA loss per order stood at Rs 381.
“In this phase of category development, we are prioritising market leadership over everything else,” Urban Company said in its shareholder letter.
The company expects margins to remain under pressure in the near term as aggressive discounting continues across the market. Urban Company said current pricing levels are unsustainable for the industry and that pricing normalisation could lead to a one-time adjustment in demand across the category.
Competition in the quick home services segment has also intensified. According to Moneycontrol, Snabbit recorded 1.51 million orders in June, while Urban Company’s InstaHelp clocked around 1.5 million orders during the month. Pronto recorded around 0.95 million orders during the same period.

title: Urban Company posts 92 Cr loss on Rs 528 Cr revenue in Q1 FY27
summary:
Home services marketplace Urban Company reported a strong 44% year-on-year growth in operating revenue in Q1 FY27. However, the company slipped into a loss of Rs 92 crore during the quarter amid its continued push for InstaHelp.
According to the company’s quarterly financial results, Urban Company's revenue from operations rose to Rs 528 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 367 crore in the same quarter last year, according to its unaudited financial results sourced from the National Stock Exchange (NSE).

The India Consumer Services business, excluding InstaHelp, remained Urban Company's largest revenue contributor, accounting for more than 67% of its operating revenue. Revenue from the segment grew 31% year-on-year to Rs 356 crore during the quarter.
The company's Native brands business recorded a 58% year-on-year increase in revenue to Rs 95 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 60 crore in the year-ago period, while its international business grew 81% to contribute Rs 65 crore.
Meanwhile, InstaHelp, Urban Company's quick-service housekeeping vertical launched in March last year, generated Rs 11.11 crore in revenue during the quarter. However, the segment reported an EBITDA loss of Rs 131.58 crore, up 11% sequentially from Rs 118.73 crore in Q4 FY26.
The company also earned Rs 38 crore from non-operating sources during the quarter, taking its overall income to Rs 566 crore. On a quarterly basis, overall revenue grew by 23% from Rs 462 crore in Q4 FY26.
On the expense side, Urban Company's employee benefit expenses rose 53% year-on-year to Rs 151 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 99 crore in the same quarter last year, while its cost of materials increased 45% to Rs 100 crore.
Finance costs, depreciation and amortisation expenses, along with other undisclosed costs, pushed the company's total expenditure to Rs 640 crore during the quarter from Rs 384 crore in Q1 FY26.
Despite strong revenue growth, Urban Company slipped to a loss of Rs 92 crore in Q1 FY27, compared to a profit of Rs 7 crore in the year-ago quarter, as it continued to make significant investments in its quick-service housekeeping vertical, InstaHelp.
At the end of Friday’s trading session, Urban Company’s shares closed 6% lower at Rs 129.39 compared to the previous closing price, taking the company’s total market capitalization to Rs 19,894 crore ($2.1 billion).

Shadowfax Technologies reported a strong performance in Q1 FY27, with the logistics and last-mile delivery firm recording a 65% year-on-year growth in operating revenue. Its profit also surged more than eightfold to Rs 65 crore during the quarter.

Shadowfax Technologies' profit surged more than eightfold to Rs 65 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 8 crore in the year-ago quarter, as the company's revenue growth continued to outpace the increase in its expenses.

Consumer appliances startup Atomberg has converted itself into a public company, marking a key milestone in its journey towards an initial public offering (IPO).
The company's shareholders have approved a special resolution to change the name of its parent entity from Atomberg Technologies Private Limited to Atomberg Technologies Limited, according to regulatory filings accessed by Entrackr.
As part of its IPO preparations, the company has appointed three independent directors: Subhasis Chaudhuri, former Director of IIT Bombay; Suman Gopalan, former CHRO at Freshworks; and Anand Vora, former CFO of UPL. summary:
Quick commerce major Zepto has postponed its IPO plans, according to multiple media reports, amid ongoing valuation discussions with investors.
The company may also raise more than Rs 1,000 crore (around $105 million) through a pre IPO placement, according to a Moneycontrol report. Existing investors including Glade Brook, General Catalyst, Goodwater Capital and Nexus Venture Partners are expected to participate in the round.
Under SEBI regulations, IPO bound companies can raise up to 20% of their proposed fresh issue through a pre IPO placement, with the amount raised adjusted against the fresh issue component of the public offering.
Zepto had originally planned to raise around Rs 8,000 crore through its IPO. In June, the company filed its updated draft red herring prospectus with SEBI for a fresh issue of Rs 8,010 crore and received the regulator's approval about a month later. The IPO size has also reportedly been trimmed to around Rs 5,000–6,000 crore
Entrackr has reached out to Zepto for comments.
The Bengaluru based company doubled its operating revenue to Rs 11,110 crore in FY26 from Rs 5,454 crore in FY25. However, its losses widened 26% to Rs 5,905 crore, making it one of the largest loss making startups in the country.
As of the end of FY26, it had current assets of Rs 9,638 crore, including cash and bank balances of Rs 973 crore.

title: Swiggy Q1 FY27 revenue jumps 37% to Rs 6,812 Cr, loss narrows 34%
summary:
Foodtech and quick commerce major Swiggy reported a 37% year-on-year increase in its operating revenue to Rs 6,812 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 4,961 crore in the year-ago quarter. The company also narrowed its losses by 34% during the period.
Scootsy Logistics, Swiggy’s supply chain and distribution arm, remained its largest revenue contributor, accounting for nearly 47% of the company’s operating revenue. Revenue from the segment rose 41% year-on-year to Rs 3,195 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 2,259 crore in the year-ago quarter.
Swiggy’s food delivery and quick commerce businesses also posted strong growth during the quarter. Revenue from food delivery increased 23% year-on-year to Rs 2,208 crore, while quick commerce arm Instamart recorded a 53% jump to Rs 1,232 crore.

The remaining operating revenue came from segments such as dine-out services and other initiatives, including Bolt and Toing.
The company also reported Rs 211 crore in other income. As a result, its total income rose to Rs 7,023 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 5,048 crore in the corresponding quarter last year.
On the expense front, procurement of materials remained Swiggy's largest cost centre at Rs 2,975 crore during the quarter. Employee benefit expenses declined marginally by 3.5% to Rs 662 crore. Advertising and sales promotion expenses stood at Rs 1,160 crore, while delivery costs amounted to Rs 1,750 crore. Other operational expenses pushed the company's total expenditure to Rs 7,813 crore in Q1 FY27.
Segment-wise, Swiggy's food delivery business remained EBITDA positive with an EBITDA of Rs 299 crore, while its quick commerce arm, Instamart, continued to incur losses and reported a negative EBITDA of Rs 651 crore during the quarter.

Swiggy's losses narrowed 34% year-on-year to Rs 791 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 1,197 crore in the corresponding quarter last year, aided by strong revenue growth.

On a sequential basis, the company's losses remained largely flat at Rs 791 crore compared with Rs 799 crore in Q4 FY26, while revenue grew 7% from Rs 6,383 crore.

Swiggy’s shares closed at Rs 295.91 on Thursday, giving the company a market capitalization of Rs 81,098 crore ($8.53 billion). 

On the competitive front, rival Eternal reported a profit of Rs 92 crore on an operating revenue of Rs 20,211 crore in Q1 FY27.

title: PhonePe launches PulsePro for enterprise market intelligence
summary:
Fullstack fintech platform PhonePe has launched PulsePro, an enterprise intelligence platform that provides businesses with market insights based on aggregated and anonymised transaction data from its payments network.
PulsePro enables enterprises to analyse consumer spending trends, category performance and local market dynamics for decisions related to expansion planning, distribution strategy, site selection and category growth. According to PhonePe, the platform offers near real time insights derived from transaction data, addressing the limitations of traditional survey based market research.
The company also shared a set of hyperlocal consumer insights generated through PulsePro. According to PhonePe, Chakan in Pune recorded the highest number of OTT users in the country, while Maharashtra led in pet related spending. Kurung Kumey district in Arunachal Pradesh reported lifestyle spending at nearly three times the state average. Jabalpur emerged as the top healthcare spending district in Madhya Pradesh, while Marathahalli in Bengaluru recorded the highest number of late night orders nationwide.
PulsePro is built on PhonePe’s payments ecosystem, which spans more than 700 million registered users, over 50 million registered merchants and 99% of India’s postal codes. It extends PhonePe Pulse, the company’s public data platform launched in 2021 for entrepreneurs, researchers, developers, policymakers and students.
While PhonePe Pulse will continue to remain free, PulsePro is positioned as a paid enterprise offering with advanced market intelligence capabilities.
The platform covers more than 200 store categories and over 100 market signals, enabling businesses to analyse spending patterns, identify growth opportunities and evaluate changes in consumer behaviour.
PulsePro also provides district and postal code level insights to support distribution planning, urban expansion, rural market prioritisation and site selection. In addition, it tracks digital commerce indicators, including quick commerce penetration at a hyperlocal level.
“Businesses today don’t just need more data, they need better intelligence. Since launching PhonePe Pulse in 2021, we have seen a growing demand from organizations looking for deeper market insights to guide expansion and strategic decision making. PhonePe PulsePro is our response to that need,” said Karthik Raghupathy, Head of Strategy at PhonePe.
According to PhonePe, PulsePro generates enterprise insights using aggregated and anonymised transaction trends while maintaining user privacy.

According to its standalone financial statements sourced from BSE, the Mumbai-based company’s revenue from operations rose to Rs 759 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 580 crore in Q1 FY26.

Founded in 2017 by Bhupinder Singh, InCred Finance is a retail-focused NBFC that provides personal loans, education loans, secured business loans, MSME financing, and lending solutions for financial institutions.
Interest income remained the company's largest revenue driver, contributing nearly 90% of its operating revenue. Revenue from this segment rose to Rs 682 crore in Q1 FY27. Fee and commission income added Rs 67 crore, while the rest came from gains on fair value changes in financial assets.
Including Rs 3 crore from non-operating income, InCred Finance's total income stood at Rs 762 crore during the quarter.
InCred Finance's loan book (excluding assigned loans) grew to Rs 14,809 crore at the end of June 2026, driven by continued momentum across its five lending verticals. The company also reported an improvement in asset quality, with gross NPAs declining to 2.0% from 2.3% a year ago and net NPAs easing to 0.7% from 0.9%. Its net worth stood at Rs 4,244 crore as of June 30, 2026.
Finance costs remained the largest expense for InCred Finance, accounting for 51% of its total expenditure. These costs rose 26% year-on-year to Rs 270 crore in Q1 FY27. Employee benefit expenses increased 39% to Rs 131 crore during the quarter.
Losses from impaired financial instruments, including loan write-offs, declined 44% year-on-year to Rs 43 crore. Depreciation charges, along with legal, collection, advertising, travel and other overheads, pushed the company's total expenditure up 15% to Rs 533 crore from Rs 465 crore in Q1 FY26.
InCred Finance's profit surged 83% year-on-year to Rs 172 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 94 crore in the year-ago quarter.

title: Peak XV makes another Go Digit exit, sells shares worth Rs 139 Cr via block deal
summary:
Peak XV Partners, an early investor in Go Digit General Insurance, has offloaded shares worth around Rs 139 crore through a block deal on the National Stock Exchange (NSE). This is its second stake sale in the company in less than two months.
 
According to NSE block deal data, Peak XV Partners, through its affiliate Peak XV Partners Growth Investments III, sold 57.21 lakh shares of Go Digit at Rs 243 share price taking the transaction value to approximately Rs 139 crore. ICICI Prudential Mutual Fund acquired the entire tranche at the same price.
 
In June, Peak XV sold 33.33 lakh shares of Go Digit for Rs 100 crore. The transaction saw participation from Aditya Birla Sun Life Mutual Fund and JPMorgan (Taiwan) Eastern Technology Fund.
 
With the latest transaction, Peak XV has sold 90.54 lakh Go Digit shares worth around Rs 239 crore across the two block deals.
 
Founded in 2017, Go Digit General Insurance offers products across motor, health, travel, property and other insurance segments. Motor insurance remains its largest business line, followed by health and fire insurance. The company counts Faering Capital, Wellington Management and TVS Capital Funds among its backers.
 
On the financial front, Go Digit’s profit after tax declined 37.5% to Rs 86.4 crore in Q1 FY27, from Rs 138.3 crore in the year-ago period. Its gross premium written also fell 8.4% to Rs 2,730.9 crore from Rs 2,981.8 crore in Q1 FY26.
 
The latest stake sale comes amid pressure on Go Digit’s stock. The insurer’s shares hit an all-time low of Rs 245 on the BSE on July 28 and have declined nearly 21% over the past month.
Go Digit’s shares were trading at Rs 252 as of 10:56 AM, taking its market capitalization to around Rs 23,430 crore.

title: Drone startup SUIND raises Rs 20.5 Cr in seed round led by Transition VC
summary:
Agriculture drone startup SUIND has raised Rs 20.5 crore ($2.2 million) in a seed funding round led by Transition VC. The round also saw participation from IIMA Ventures.
Entrackr had exclusively reported the development recently. 
The fresh capital will be used to scale the commercial deployment of its agriculture drone platform, accelerate the development of its autonomous surveillance and infrastructure inspection drone, strengthen its proprietary autonomy technology and expand its engineering team.
Founded in 2020 by Kunal Shrivastava and Kevin Kleber, SUIND develops autonomous unmanned aerial systems that use computer vision for navigation instead of relying primarily on GPS. Its technology enables drones to operate in low-altitude and GPS-denied environments.
The startup has commercially deployed its DGCA-certified autonomous spraying drone, Bumblebee, across farms and plantations. It is also developing WASP, an autonomous aerial platform for industrial monitoring, security, surveillance and defence applications.
Over the next 12 to 24 months, SUIND plans to scale the manufacturing and deployment of Bumblebee while preparing WASP for commercial launch. The agriculture drone ecosystem in India has witnessed growing interest in recent years, driven by demand for precision farming and government support for drone adoption. Suind competes with startups such as Marut Drones, Garuda Aerospace, IoTechWorld Avigation, BharatRohan, and Dhaksha Unmanned Systems.

title: Indian Physical AI attracts $155 Mn in 2026 as robotics, real-world data gain traction
summary:
Home services startup Pronto’s decision to expand its Physical AI experiment involving wearable cameras inside customers’ homes has brought the emerging technology into focus, particularly the opportunity around real-world data for training AI and robotics systems.
The move comes even as larger home services players Snabbit and Urban Company's InstaHelp have opted out of similar initiatives. Pronto, which has raised $45 million in funding this year alone, is expanding its opt-in Pronto Verified service, which records service sessions and uses anonymized footage for AI training. As companies explore ways to collect real-world data for AI and robotics, investor interest is also growing across robotics, autonomous systems, AI-powered hardware, and training infrastructure.
Year-on-year funding trend
According to data compiled by Entrackr, startups in the Indian Physical AI ecosystem have raised around $155 million across 31 deals in 2026 so far. This compares with $130 million across 25 deals in 2025, $124 million across 24 deals in 2024, and $91 million across 21 deals in 2023, according to Venture Intelligence data.

For this analysis, the funding dataset includes startups headquartered in India, as well as overseas companies with significant Physical AI product development, commercial deployment, or data collection in India. Companies with only engineering or support teams in India, or where Physical AI remains an experimental or ancillary initiative, such as Pronto, are excluded from the funding tally.
Funding in 2026 so far is already about 19% higher than the total raised in 2025 and more than 70% above 2023 levels. Most companies that raised capital this year are early-stage ventures, though capital remains concentrated among a few larger rounds. Innefu Labs, Unbox Robotics, and Deccan AI together raised $83 million, accounting for more than half of the $155 million raised so far.
Perhaps predictably, this remains the safest bet on the AI boom, in terms of predictable, if relatively tiny part of it. With firms building their own layers on top of existing frontier AI networks or otherwise. Some would say this is just as well, pointing to the havoc the rise in valuations, followed by the crash it has caused in South Korea this month.
Growth-stage deals lead the pack
Innefu Labs led the segment with a $30 million Series B round led by Panthera Growth Partners. The national security-focused AI company is also building a dedicated Physical AI and robotics division for defence and security applications.
Supply chain robotics startup Unbox Robotics raised $28 million in a round led by ICICI Venture, with participation from RedStartLabs, F Prime, 3one4 Capital, Navam Capital, Force Ventures, and existing investors.
Deccan AI raised $25 million in a Series A round led by A91 Partners, with participation from SIG and Prosus Ventures. The startup provides data and model training, post-training data, and evaluation services for frontier AI labs, and has expanded into enterprise AI solutions.
Outside the funding dataset, US-based physical security AI startup Hakimo, founded by Indian-origin entrepreneurs Sam Joseph and Sagar Honnungar, raised $12 million in a growth round led by Zigg Capital, with participation from Neotribe Ventures, Vertex Ventures, Defy.vc, and Rocketship.vc. It uses AI to automate physical security monitoring through existing camera infrastructure.
Early-stage startups gain momentum
Marine robotics company Rekise Marine raised $9.7 million in a seed round co-led by Accel and NKSquared. It builds autonomous ships and submarines and partners with Indian shipyards for vessel design and integration.
San Francisco and Bengaluru-based Human Archive raised $8.2 million in a round led by Wing Venture Capital and NVP Capital. The Y Combinator-backed company came into the spotlight in India following early talks with Snabbit around a potential Physical AI initiative, though the home services startup eventually decided not to proceed. Human Archive is building large-scale human sensorimotor datasets to train robots and Physical AI systems.
Bengaluru-based SwitchOn raised $8 million in a pre-Series B round led by IvyCap Ventures. The startup develops AI-powered vision systems for automated quality inspection across manufacturing production lines.
Other notable rounds include Spector.ai’s $6.7 million raise led by IvyCap Ventures and ANSCER Robotics’ $5.4 million (Rs 45 crore) Series A led by IAN Alpha Fund, with participation from Info Edge.
Bengaluru and Detroit-based Mowito raised $3 million in a pre-seed round led by Version One Ventures to build AI foundation models that enable industrial robotic arms to learn manufacturing tasks through demonstrations. Construction-focused Physical AI and robotics startup Flo Mobility raised $2.5 million in a pre-Series A round co-led by Mela Ventures and Arali Ventures.
The remaining funding was spread across more than 20 deeptech and robotics startups, including AutoVRse, WorkOnGrid, RoshAI, Armatrix, Constems, and others. The investor base across these deals includes mainstream venture and growth funds such as Accel, A91 Partners, ICICI Venture, IvyCap Ventures, 3one4 Capital, Prosus Ventures, SIG, Info Edge, and Version One Ventures. 
The data layer around Physical AI
A separate set of companies is working on the data collection, annotation, and training infrastructure required for Physical AI systems. Human Archive is building human sensorimotor datasets for robots and Physical AI systems, while Neocambrian AI has launched an India-focused robotics data factory. Other companies working across this layer in India include iMerit, Human Stryde, Luel, Awign, Build, Centific, Humyn Labs, Aura ML, Build AI, FPV Labs, and Northstar.
Physical AI models require real-world data that captures human actions, objects, environments, and interactions. Much of this data has to be collected specifically for robotics and embodied AI use cases rather than sourced from existing internet datasets.
Pronto offers another example of how such data could be generated. While the company is not included in the $155 million Physical AI funding tally, its experiment shows how businesses with workers operating in real-world environments could become a source of training data.
Larger rounds could follow
Skylark Labs, led by India-born founder and CEO Amarjot Singh, has a significant India presence and works with the country’s defence ecosystem, including the Indian Army, Indian Air Force, and ideaForge. The company is in talks to raise $100–150 million at a valuation of more than $1 billion.
If completed, the round would be substantially larger than any individual Physical AI funding round involving an India-linked company in 2026.
Physical AI companies, particularly those building hardware, will still have to deal with higher deployment costs and longer commercial cycles. For companies collecting real-world data, privacy and consent will remain key concerns, especially for data collected inside homes.

title: Kissht clocks Rs 670 Cr revenue and Rs 95 Cr profit in Q1 FY27
summary:
Digital lending platform Kissht reported its first quarterly results for the fiscal year ending March 2027. The company's operating revenue grew 45% year-on-year in the quarter, while its profit increased 58% to Rs 95 crore.
Kissht’s revenue from operations increased to Rs 670 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 463 crore in Q1 FY26, according to its consolidated financial statement sourced from NSE.
Founded in 2015 by Ranvir Singh and Krishnan Vishwanathan, provides small-ticket consumer loans and has scaled aggressively through partnerships with merchants across electronics, fashion, travel, and other categories. The company primarily earns interest income from these loans, although a detailed revenue breakup for the quarter was not disclosed.
The company also earned Rs 7 crore from non operating sources, raising its total revenue to Rs 677 crore.
Kissht continued to expand its lending business during the quarter, with its assets under management (AUM) growing 61% year-on-year and 13% sequentially to Rs 8,001 crore. The company has cumulatively served over 12.25 million customers, a 26% increase from a year ago. Its off-book AUM stood at Rs 4,284 crore, accounting for 53.6% of the total portfolio, reflecting its capital-light partnership model.
Impairment on financial instruments remained one of the largest expense heads for the fintech platform, accounting for over 23% of the total cost base. The expense grew 28% year on year to Rs 128 crore in Q1 FY27, while finance costs increased 39% to Rs 82 crore.
Employee benefit expenses stood at Rs 71 crore, while spending on marketing, legal and professional services, and IT expenses drove the company's total expenditure up 42% year on year to Rs 549 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 386 crore in the same quarter last year.
In the end, strong revenue growth helped the Mumbai-based company post a 58% year-on-year increase in profit to Rs 95 crore in Q1 FY27. On a sequential basis, profit rose 16% from Rs 82 crore in the preceding quarter (Q4 FY26).
At the close of trading on Wednesday, Kissht's shares were priced at Rs 343.45, giving the company a market capitalization of Rs 5,796 crore ($610 million).

title: TBO Tek’s Q1 FY27 revenue jumps 81% to Rs 926 Cr; profit grows 32%
summary:
Travel distribution platform TBO Tek reported an 81.2% year-on-year growth in its operating revenue for the first quarter of FY27, while its profit increased 31.7% during the same period.
The company’s revenue from operations rose to Rs 926 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 511 crore in Q1 FY26, according to its unaudited financial results filed with the National Stock Exchange (NSE).


 
Hotel and package bookings remained TBO Tek’s largest revenue stream, contributing Rs 800 crore in Q1 FY27, up 89.1% from Rs 423 crore in the corresponding quarter last year. Revenue from air ticketing increased marginally to Rs 81 crore from Rs 78 crore, while other operating revenue climbed to Rs 45 crore from Rs 10.4 crore.
Including Rs 13 crore in other income, the company’s total income stood at Rs 939 crore in Q1 FY27, compared to Rs 524 crore in Q1 FY26.
On a sequential basis, operating revenue grew 13.8% from Rs 814 crore in Q4 FY26.
On the expense front, service fees remained the largest cost component, rising to Rs 373 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 178 crore in the year-ago quarter. Employee benefit expenses increased to Rs 179 crore, while depreciation and finance costs stood at Rs 33 crore and Rs 15 crore, respectively.
Overall expenditure grew 83.1% to Rs 835 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 456 crore in Q1 FY26.
Despite higher expenses, TBO Tek’s profit increased to Rs 83 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 63 crore in Q1 FY26. On a quarter-on-quarter basis, profit rose 38.3% from Rs 60 crore in Q4 FY26.
TBO Tek’s share price closed at Rs 1,522.60, with a total market capitalization of Rs 16,385 crore.
